title: The retail vaccine limb in the statute and the regulations' separate vaccine item
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(c)(5) limits retail collaborative practice to, among other things, administration of vaccines or the modification of dosages of medications prescribed by the supervising physician for asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, congestive heart failure, HIV or AIDS, osteoporosis and co-morbidities identified by the supervising physician for the individual patient along with the primary diagnosis. The statute's words do not state separately whether the list of conditions reaches the vaccine limb; if it does, it reaches it only through the words prescribed by the supervising physician for, so on that reading the vaccine is one the supervising physician prescribed for a named condition or identified co-morbidity. 247 CMR 16.03(5)(b) and 243 CMR 2.12(4)(e)2. state vaccine administration as a separate item: pharmacists, as authorized pursuant to a collaborative practice agreement, may administer vaccines, with no disease list and no requirement of a supervising-physician prescription. Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B3/4 the rules and regulations shall govern each collaborative practice agreement and shall be defined and limited by section 24B1/2, chapter 94C and other applicable statutes.
exam_relevance: Tests which retail vaccine course meets the narrowest reading of clause (5) as well as the regulations: an agreement authorizing vaccine administration and referencing the disease state, a referred, notified and consenting patient 18 or older, and a vaccine the supervising physician prescribed for a named condition or identified co-morbidity; and that a vaccine given without that prescription or unrelated to those conditions rests on the regulations' reading.

authority.name: Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations
Board of Registration in Medicine regulations

common_confusions: Treating a vaccine for a named condition the agreement references as within clause (5) on every reading without a supervising-physician prescription: on the reading that the list reaches vaccines, the words prescribed by the supervising physician for attach as well.
Treating the regulations' authorization pursuant to a collaborative practice agreement as supplying the statute's words prescribed by the supervising physician.
Treating the statute as settling whether its list of conditions reaches the vaccine limb; its words do not state it separately.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, ss. 24B1/2 and 24B3/4 on malegislature.gov and in the current mass.gov PDFs of 247 CMR 16.00 and 243 CMR 2.00 on 2026-09-17.
